text: Training Expectations - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe Training Expectations - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Teresa Torres 13 Oct 2026 14 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts You've got twelve people and one hour booked at next week's offsite. Can someone teach your team to do continuous discovery in that hour? Teresa Torres's answer is a flat no — and this episode is about why. Petra Wille and Teresa Torres unpack one of the most common requests they get during offsite-and-strategy season: "Can you teach my team continuous discovery in a single session?" Petra often gets requests like this: "We want our product people to take more ownership. Could you do a keynote at our all-hands that gets that going?" The problem, they argue, is a mismatch — people ask for a service (a talk, a workshop) expecting a benefit (a capable, habit-driven team) that the service simply can't deliver. They separate know-how from skill, explain why real capability is built in a "gym" of repeated practice rather than a one-hour download, and get honest about what a talk, a four-hour workshop, and a full coaching program can each realistically achieve. If you're the one buying — or delivering — team training, this is a practical guide to calibrating expectations before anyone books the room. Key Takeaways Continuous discovery isn't one skill you pick up in a workshop — it's many skills, habits, and mindsets built through repeated practice. The core mismatch: people request a service (a talk) expecting a benefit (a capable team) that service can't deliver. Know-how transfers fast; skills and mindset shifts require a "gym" — practice over time, not a one-hour download. A talk's real job is to inspire, plant a seed, and paint a picture of a different future — not to change behavior on its own. Talks deliver most when they're embedded in a longer coaching or training program. Providers need to communicate the full picture of what mastery takes — even though an honest picture can feel "too hard." You don't have to become an expert to get real value from the habits. Open Q&A often surfaces the organizational barriers that must be addressed before any training can work. Notable Moments "That's like saying, can you teach me how to be a marketer in an hour?" — Teresa "The people that are asking for training don't know enough about discovery to know even what training they need." — Teresa "We need to build the gym and go there." — Petra "Our job is to paint a picture of a different future. It doesn't create that future." — Teresa "I'm not poo-pooing the one-hour talk. I'm poo-pooing the one-hour talk as the silver bullet that changes your team's behavior." — Teresa Resources & Links: Follow Teresa Torres: https://ProductTalk.org Follow Petra Wille: https://Petra-Wille.com Mentioned in this episode: Continuous Discovery Habits by Teresa Torres — the source of the "13 habits" referenced throughout Product Discovery Basics: Everything You Need to Know The What & Why of Continuous Discovery — Teresa's one-hour overview talk Managing-Up!
